intent: Phase 1: gator-preferences-v1 contract + discriminated reader + validator
notes: New contract `gator-preferences-v1` for the unified machine-local preferences file at `~/.gator/preferences.json`. This plan (`.gator/vault/artifacts/2026-08-29-machine-python-preference-implementation-plan.md` r3) implements the `python:` section of Sketch B's unified-preferences architecture; the reserved `hooks:` stub is documented in the schema so the follow-on hook-mode plan can extend the same file additively without a v2 bump.

`contracts/schemas/gator-preferences-v1.json`: schema with three sections (`python:` fully specified, `hooks:` reserved stub, `notes` free-form), `additionalProperties: true` at every level for additive forward-compat. Only `schema` is required.

`contracts/compatibility/test_preferences_schema.py` (13 tests, 12 pass + 1 machine-local skip): validates schema conformance, additive-friendliness, and forward-compat cases (missing python section, hooks-only file, unknown top-level section tolerated). Follows the pattern from `test_runtime_pin.py`.
`contracts/compatibility/fixtures/valid_preferences.json`: canonical fixture populated with the field-report example (LocalAppData py.exe path).

`gator_core.read_preferences()` returns a **discriminated result**: `{"state": "absent"}` / `{"state": "malformed", "reason": ...}` / `{"state": "present", "data": {...}}`. The distinction is the load-bearing fix for r1 whiteboard finding 1 — collapsing to `Optional[dict]` would make the "invalid override refuses loudly, no fallback" invariant unenforceable for the malformed-file case. BOM-tolerant (`utf-8-sig`, same pattern as `resolve_governed_runtime`). Never raises. Both copies.

`gator_core._validate_launcher_candidate(path, for_shebang=True)` returns `(valid, reason)` with reasons `empty-path` / `relative-path` / `basename-mismatch: <got>` / `spaced-path` / `file-not-found`. Existence checked LAST so configuration reasons surface even when the file is missing. Both copies.
`os` added to gator_core.py imports (both copies) — needed for `os.path.isabs/isfile/basename`.
